title: The percussionists: Sue Evans, Palmer Lambkin and Airto
summary: Gil describes his drummer and percussionists, including Sue Evans, Palmer Lambkin and Airto Moreira.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Then I have percussion. (Sue Evans, you saw her?)?
Yes. Where did you find her?

Well she was a student of a percussion player that I'd had before that. She has been studying drums with him since she was nine. And she's like a regular accomplished drummer, you know. She can play the drums. She knows all about drums. She's been taking lessons for about ten years every week. So she's really like a basic drummer. There's no fooling around about her.
Isn't that something? And for a young girl to be able to play with you. (LAUGHTER). Now she is a fantastic girl. (LAUGHTER).
She works on the road with Judy Collins, the jazz singer.
Yes. She's been on the road recently. (?).

She gets $250 a concert, so if she goes out for a few days each week it can give her a thousand, you know, save it up. She does it for a few people a couple of months of the year. Yes, that's what she's doing now. She's just luckily back in town for Monday.

Then I have another percussionist who is a friend of mine and he's a composer really and a vibraphonist but he's just around a lot and all of a sudden I got the idea having him play some percussion too. His name is Palmer Lambkin.
Yes, He was there, he was fine.
He came on during the second half I believe, didn't he?

That's Airto McIerid (Airto), that's Airto. He's from Brazil. He's a Brazilian percussionist and his wife Flora, they are both from Brazil. Airto was with Miles Davis for a couple of years until recently. Now he's with (Chick Corea) and he's very very good.
Every time they hear I'm going to play somewhere they come dashing down with their little box of things and play. They are ready to play with the band. (LAUGHTER).

But the other fellow, Palmer Lambkin, he's a composer and he'll be heard from one of these days. He's very serious about it and good. That's all the rhythm now. That's all the instruments that are not wind instruments. Those are all, that's like, oh there's Bruce (Bitwas) the regular drummer who plays the #traps# And the two percussion players, Palmer Lambkin and Sue Evans and (Airto) sometimes. And & Dick Horowitz & on the synthesizer and Ted
